question: A and B complete a work in 15 days. B alone takes 25 days. In how many days will A alone complete the work?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the formula: Days for A alone = (X × Y) ÷ (Y − X)

Here, X = (A + B) combined days = 15, Y = B alone days = 25

Time for A = (15 × 25) ÷ (25 − 15) = 375 ÷ 10 = 37.5 days

**∴ Answer = 37.5 days**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by A and B together = 15 days

Time taken by B alone = 25 days

**Formula used:**

Total Work = LCM of all given days

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Number of Days

Efficiency of A = (Efficiency of A + B) − (Efficiency of B)

Efficiency of A = 5 − 3 = 2 units/day

**Calculations:**

Total units of work to be completed by A = 75 units

⇒ Time taken by A alone = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of A ⇒ Time taken by A alone = 75 ÷ 2 ⇒ Time taken by A alone = 37.5 days

**∴ The correct answer is 37.5 days (Option 1).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inverse Relation of Time and Efficiency

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken. If the efficiency ratio of A and B is x : y, then the time taken ratio is y : x.

Combined Work Formula

If A can do a piece of work in 'a' days and B can do it in 'b' days, they together finish the work in (a × b) ÷ (a + b) days.

Pipes and Cisterns Analogy

The same logic applies to pipes filling a tank. If one pipe fills a tank in x hours and a leak empties it in y hours, the net rate is (1/x − 1/y).

Work and Wages

Total wages are always distributed in the ratio of the work done, which is (Efficiency × Time) for each individual.
